items.problem: The migration bootstrap copied stale UWP build output (.NET-Native ILC *.g.cs from sub-project bin/obj) into the WinUI 3 target tree, which the SDK-style csproj **/*.cs glob then compiled, producing 173,913 build errors (CS0101/CS0227/CS0234 + WMC9999). The app never built or launched; final score 0/100.
items.evidence: winui-build-first-errors.txt (CS0101 'already contains a definition for Interop_mincore_CPINFOEXW...' from AppServicesClient/obj\x64\Release\ilc and AppServicesProvider/bin|obj\...\ilc); migration-score.json winui_build_status='failed: dotnet build returned 173913 errors ... stale UWP .NET-Native ILC .g.cs ... swept into the WinUI csproj **/*.cs glob'; session-log.txt L1339-1342 + TURN 60-64 build hang >600s.
items.skill_search: Grepped winui-uwp-migration for: bin, obj, ilc, .g.cs, EnableDefaultCompileItems, 'Compile Remove', copy-exclude. Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 Step 1 (L60-85) copy had NO bin/obj exclusion; Step 3 (L106), Validate-UwpMigration.ps1 (L81), Test-AppLaunch.ps1 (L115) all DO exclude bin/obj. No build-error doc covered the duplicate-type/ilc case.
items.wrong_text_if_any: Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 L60 '# ─── 1. Copy source files (everything except .csproj)' followed by `Get-ChildItem -Path $Source -Recurse -File ... | Where-Object { ...extension match only... }` with no directory exclusion.
items.root_cause: Step 1's copy filters only by file extension, not by directory, so it imports build artifacts from any previously-built UWP source. MSBuild's default bin/obj exclusion only covers the project-root bin/obj, so nested sub-project copies are compiled.
items.proposed_fix: Add the same $excludeDirs (bin, obj, .vs, .git, .github, .copilot, packages, node_modules) directory filter to the Step 1 copy in Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 so build output is never copied. Add a MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md 'Common build errors' entry describing the CS0101/CS0227 flood from *\obj\...\ilc\*.g.cs and the 'delete copied bin/obj' fix as a backstop.
items.generalizes: Every UWP project that has been built (most have) leaves bin/obj artifacts; the bootstrap copies them for any scenario. Multi-project samples make it worse because nested bin/obj escape MSBuild's project-root-only default exclusion. Preventing the copy fixes the entire class of scenarios, not just AppServices.
